The ladder therefore begins at the three people who do not know where the Two of Swords went.

Bullet 1 names Naruru, Teigero-Bangero and Panta-Putta in a bare comma list with no order and no locations. They are read as an unordered set and share a group so all three draw at once; a strict ladder would mark whichever I happened to put first and hide the other two. But the page gives NO zone for any of them -- the categories mention Lower Jeuno, and categories are not walkthrough text, so inventing a zone from them would be exactly the guessing this pipeline exists to avoid. Those three rows therefore carry a null zone, which means they match anywhere, and that is why the quest is medium rather than high. None of the three folds to an ambiguous NPC key, so the zone-less rows are merely broad, not structurally forbidden.

notes:
A two-rung repeatable fetch, and the only interesting thing on the page is the OR. The header ('Two Velkk Masks or Two Velkk Necklaces') and bullet 2 ('two Velkk Necklace or two Velkk Mask') agree: either pair works, and they do not mix -- it is two of one kind, not any two. That is exactly what items / items_alt expresses, so two Velkk Necklace go in items and two Velkk Mask in items_alt, and items_partial stays false because nothing was left unexpressed.

Both rungs are the same NPC in the same place, which the runtime collapses to one marker with readiness looking ahead across them; that is correct here, since walking up to Veldeth with the shells in hand is the whole quest. Nothing is observable: the reward is 500 experience and 300 Bayld, neither of which is an item, and the masks and necklaces are what you bring rather than what you get.

The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section holds one sentence -- repeating the quest does not move Adoulin fame -- which is a cooldown-style remark and not a step, so no rung comes from it. Fame 'Seekers of Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions the addon knows, so region is null and raw carries the string. The page carries the wiki's own [unverified] marker, which is flagged rather than hidden.
